results.answer: Fold the Armor branch into the maths — the app DOES know the affixture. Affixing writes `attachedTo: hostId` on the spellheart's inventory entry (play.ts:747) and the host's `itemType` says armor vs weapon (attachments.ts:59-66), so gate the Armor benefits (+2 item Athletics, resistance 10 nonlethal) on `attachedTo` resolving to an armor host and put them in passiveEffects, not in the situational registry: ruling B's rule is that an unrestricted flat bonus belongs in the total and only a rules-restricted one becomes a star, and 'while affixed to armor' is a build state, not a moment. The Weapon branch (+1d8 piercing until the end of your next turn after Activating) is a timed post-activation effect -> an item-driven mode (ModeDef.fromItemId/duration, types.ts:1386-1403), not a star. ⚠ Blocking gap to fix first: affixing sets worn/equipped/invested all false (play.ts:747) while every item lane gates on `worn || equipped || invested` (derive.ts:707, explain.ts:195/219) — so an affixed spellheart or talisman currently contributes nothing anywhere. Widen those gates to count `attachedTo`.

results.why: Option (a) — render the fake +2 as if real — is off the table on evidence: the registry is display-of-what-you-actually-have, ruling H.3 refused to model Demon's Knot's penalty on the wearer because the text says it does not apply, and the app already prints the item's full description (which states 'It does neither'), so there is no GM secret left to protect. What is NOT settled anywhere is whether a cursed item that grants nothing should be visibly FLAGGED as cursed or pass in silence — that is a house-style call about how the app talks to the player, and it will govern every cursed item in the game, not just this one.
